panels.title: Block tip age
panels.description: now() - latest_block_timestamp

panels.title: Blocks indexed per second (by fetcher)
panels.description: rate of block_full_processing_duration_microseconds_count — one observation per block processed

panels.title: Transactions per second (by fetcher)
panels.description: rate of transactions_imported_count — incremented in Indexer.Block.Fetcher.import/2 on each successful block import

panels.title: Internal transactions per second
panels.description: rate of internal_transactions_imported_count — incremented on each successful import in Indexer.Fetcher.InternalTransaction

panels.title: Logs per second (by fetcher)
panels.description: rate of logs_imported_count — incremented in Indexer.Block.Fetcher.import/2 on each successful block import

panels.title: Blocks imported per second (by fetcher)
panels.description: rate of blocks_imported_count — incremented in Indexer.Block.Fetcher.import/2 by the block batch size on each successful import. Block-level analogue of transactions_imported_count.

panels.title: Blocks internal-tx-indexed per second
panels.description: rate of blocks_internal_transactions_indexed_count — incremented in Indexer.Fetcher.InternalTransaction by the unique block count of each successful batch. Block-level analogue of internal_transactions_imported_count.

panels.title: Block range end-to-end latency (per range: fetch + parse + import)
panels.description: block_full_processing_duration_microseconds — wall-clock from JSON-RPC fetch start to Chain.import end for ONE block range (a batch of blocks). INCLUDED: block JSON-RPC fetch, receipt fetch, parsing, address extraction, Chain.import for all blocks/txs/logs/tokens in the range. NOT divided per-block, so this value scales with range size — for per-block DB write time see the Chain.import latency panel to the right. avg = rate(_sum)/rate(_count). last-max = max_over_time(_last[…]) sampled at scrape time; brief outliers between scrapes may be missed.

panels.title: Block Chain.import latency (per-block average)
panels.description: block_import_duration_microseconds — Chain.import wall-clock for blocks/txs/logs/balances DIVIDED BY no_blocks_to_import (per-block average). A batch of 50 blocks finishing in 50ms shows as 1ms/block — sub-millisecond values are real and expected for fast batches. To get the per-call DB time, multiply by the batch size from `blocks_imported_count` rate vs `block_full_processing_count` rate. Includes DB-pool checkout, BEGIN, all upserts (and any row-lock waits), and COMMIT.

panels.title: Block JSON-RPC fetch latency (HTTP only)
panels.description: block_batch_fetch_request_duration_microseconds — HTTP round-trip + JSON decode by EthereumJSONRPC for `eth_getBlockByNumber` batches. Excludes receipt fetch, parsing, transformation, and Chain.import. Per-range, not per-block.

panels.title: Chain.import latency — internal-tx batch (avg / last-max)
panels.description: internal_transactions_import_duration_microseconds_* — wall-clock duration of one Chain.import call per internal-tx batch (success or failure). Avg = rate(_sum)/rate(_count). last-max = max_over_time(_last[…]) sampled at scrape time; brief outliers between scrapes may be missed. Use the gate_hold panel below for tail-resistant visibility on the same critical section. Climbing avg = Postgres or the parallel sub-multi fan-out inside Chain.import is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Missing data (blocks / internal txs / token balances)
Indexed tip vs node tip
panels.description: latest_block_number is the indexer's tip; node tip = indexer + delay_from_last_node_block-equivalent block. Plot both side by side.

panels.title: Internal-tx indexing errors by block range (100k bucket)
panels.description: Heatmap of rate(internal_transactions_indexing_errors_count) summed across stages, by 100k-block bucket. Row label is reconstructed to the bucket's starting block number by appending 5 zeros to the block_range_100k bucket value (e.g. bucket 132 → label 13200000 = blocks 13,200,000–13,299,999). Bright cells = blocks in that range currently failing internal-tx indexing (RPC or DB). Pair with the stage breakdown to identify root cause, and with `SELECT min/max(block_number) FROM pending_block_operations` to confirm the stuck range.

panels.title: Internal-tx indexing errors by stage
panels.description: rate(internal_transactions_indexing_errors_count) broken down by stage (rpc_fetch vs db_import). Tells you whether the node or the database is the bottleneck — the heatmap to the left shows where in the chain.

panels.title: Phase 1 — raw HTTP fetch latency (avg / last-max)
panels.description: internal_transactions_raw_fetch_duration_microseconds — HTTP round-trip only, NO gunzip / NO Jason.decode. Should be much smaller than the legacy `Internal-tx fetch (JSON-RPC) latency` panel. If avg climbs here the RPC node is the bottleneck; if it stays flat while throughput drops, look at phase 2.

panels.title: Decode + transform latency — gate sub-step (avg / last-max)
panels.description: internal_transactions_decode_duration_microseconds — gunzip + Jason.decode + trace flattening + transform. Runs INSIDE the HeavyStageGate permit but this metric measures ONLY the decode sub-step. The same permit is also held during the subsequent Chain.import for internal-tx — see the "Gate hold vs decode vs Chain.import" panel below for the full picture. Knob: INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_HEAVY_PERMITS bounds concurrency.

panels.title: Heavy-stage gate wait (avg / last-max)
panels.description: internal_transactions_heavy_gate_wait_duration_microseconds — time a BufferedTask task spends parked at HeavyStageGate before acquiring a permit. Sustained nonzero values = gate is the bottleneck. Knobs: raise INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_HEAVY_PERMITS (more memory) or lower INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_CONCURRENCY / BATCH_SIZE (less pipeline pressure).

panels.title: Heavy-stage gate permits in use
panels.description: internal_transactions_heavy_gate_in_use gauge — number of decode/import slots currently held. Plateaus at INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_HEAVY_PERMITS when saturated. If this is consistently below the permit count, the gate isn't the bottleneck — look at RPC fetch or DB import latency instead.

panels.title: Gate hold vs decode vs Chain.import — what the permit really protects
panels.description: The HeavyStageGate permit is held from acquisition through decode + Chain.import + small bookkeeping. This panel plots all three avgs: decode (lowest), Chain.import (middle), gate_hold (top). decode + Chain.import should roughly equal gate_hold — any visible gap above their sum is the unmeasured pre/post-import work that the gate is also serializing. The gate's stated purpose is memory containment for decoded trace responses, so holding it through Chain.import is the main source of gate-serialization beyond its design intent. "last-max" on gate_hold is max_over_time of the latest-value gauge sampled at scrape time; brief outliers between scrapes may be missed. Avg = rate(_sum)/rate(_count).

panels.title: Raw response body size — compressed (avg / last-max, bytes)
panels.description: internal_transactions_raw_body_bytes — size of each debug_traceBlockByNumber HTTP body (compressed if ETHEREUM_JSONRPC_HTTP_GZIP_ENABLED=true, else uncompressed). Bounds the memory held by parked tasks waiting on HeavyStageGate. Spiking last-max = recent responses are large — consider lowering INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_BATCH_SIZE.

panels.title: Decompressed body size (avg / last-max, bytes)
panels.description: internal_transactions_decompressed_body_bytes — size of each debug_traceBlockByNumber response after gunzip, one observation per HTTP round-trip. Peak Elixir-term memory during decode ≈ last-max × HeavyStageGate permits. Divide by the compressed panel's avg for the wire-compression ratio (typically 10–50× for trace payloads).

panels.title: Buffer queue size
panels.description: Total items the InternalTransaction BufferedTask currently holds in memory across current_buffer, current_front_buffer and bound_queue. Near zero for an extended period while indexing is supposed to be active = BufferedTask is starved (typically poll:false + no block imports calling async_fetch). A restart re-runs init and refills.

panels.title: Buffer block — min
panels.description: Lowest block_number currently held in the BufferedTask's in-memory state.

panels.title: Buffer block — max
panels.description: Highest block_number currently held in the BufferedTask's in-memory state.

panels.title: Last indexed block
panels.description: Highest block_number from the most recently imported internal-tx batch. Flat line while pipeline stages are non-zero = imports stalled. With FETCH_ORDER=desc this hugs the chain tip as a freshly populated batch always carries the highest available block.

panels.title: Buffer queue size over time
panels.description: Total items the BufferedTask is holding in memory. Drops to zero while indexing is supposed to be active = starvation: init's one-shot stream completed and nothing is refilling the buffer.

panels.title: Buffer block range + last indexed
panels.description: Min and max block_number currently held in the BufferedTask's in-memory state, plus the last successfully imported block. With FETCH_ORDER=desc the buffer max stays near chain tip and the min drifts down as catchup progresses.

panels.title: Stage time spent per second (worker-equivalents)
panels.description:
Each series shows concurrent work-units per wall-second. A value of N means the stage is doing N workers' worth of work. Compare to each stage's concurrency limit (block fetcher pool, INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_CONCURRENCY, INDEXER_INTERNAL_TRANSACTIONS_HEAVY_PERMITS, DB pool) to spot the bottleneck.

Mixed sources: most series use sum(rate(<metric>_sum))/1e6 — completion-based, accurate for fast stages (block_import, block_batch_fetch, itx_raw_fetch, itx_decode). The itx_import line uses the real-time internal_transactions_heavy_gate_in_use gauge instead, because Chain.import for internal-tx can run for minutes and sum-based saturation lags reality by 100×+ for that stage. The gauge reflects how many permits are currently held (≈ in-flight Chain.import calls, since Chain.import dominates gate hold time).
